# Ezekiel 12 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The word of the LORD came to me:

**2** "Son of man, you dwell in the midst of a rebellious house, who have eyes to see, but see not, who have ears to hear, but hear not, for they are a rebellious house.

**3** As for you, son of man, prepare for yourself an exile's baggage, and go into exile by day in their sight. You shall go like an exile from your place to another place in their sight. Perhaps they will understand, though they are a rebellious house.

**4** You shall bring out your baggage by day in their sight, as baggage for exile, and you shall go out yourself at evening in their sight, as those do who must go into exile.

**5** In their sight dig through the wall, and bring your baggage out through it.

**6** In their sight you shall lift the baggage upon your shoulder and carry it out at dusk. You shall cover your face, that you may not see the land, for I have made you a sign for the house of Israel."

**7** And I did as I was commanded. I brought out my baggage by day, as baggage for exile, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my own hands. I went out in the dark, carrying my belongings on my shoulder in their sight.

**8** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**9** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**10** Say to them, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: This oracle concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are in it.'

**11** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**12** And the prince who is among them shall lift his baggage upon his shoulder at dusk, and shall go out. They shall dig through the wall to bring things out through it. He shall cover his face, that he may not see the land with his eyes.

**13** And I will spread My net over him, and he shall be taken in My snare. And I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, and he shall die there.

**14** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**15** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**16** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**17** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**18** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**19** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**20** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**21** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**22** "Son of man, what is this proverb that you have about the land of Israel, saying, 'The days grow long, and every vision comes to nothing'?

**23** Tell them therefore, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: I will put an end to this proverb, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel.' But say to them, 'The days are near, and the fulfillment of every vision.'

**24** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**25** For I am the LORD; I will speak the word that I will speak, and it will be performed. It will no longer be delayed, but in your days, O rebellious house, I will speak the word and perform it, declares the Lord GOD."

**26** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**27** And the LORD declared concerning the exile and the fulfillment of His word against the rebellious house of Israel.

**28** Therefore say to them, 'Thus says the Lord GOD: None of My words will be delayed any longer, but the word that I speak will be performed, declares the Lord GOD.'"

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **12:3-6**: This sign-act specifically predicts King Zedekiah's attempted escape from Jerusalem in 586 BCE. The digging through the wall, covered face, and shoulder-bag all correspond to the historical event.

- **12:13**: The paradox — brought to Babylon but 'shall not see it' — was precisely fulfilled when Zedekiah was blinded by Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah before transport to Babylon.

- **12:22-28**: The section addresses prophetic credibility. Delayed fulfillment does not mean failed prophecy — it means God's patience, which the cynical proverb misreads as impotence.

— LOGOS
